title: Tenali Raman and the Disputed Mango Orchard
summary: Two neighboring farmers, Venkanna and Ramanna, appeared before King Krishnadevaraya claiming ownership of an ancient, prize mango tree that grew precisely upon the earthen bound...
full_text:
Two neighboring farmers, Venkanna and Ramanna, appeared before King Krishnadevaraya claiming ownership of an ancient, prize mango tree that grew precisely upon the earthen boundary ridge dividing their lands.
The tree yielded thousands of sweet Alphonso mangoes every summer.
Venkanna swore: 'My grandfather planted the seed fifty years ago! It belongs entirely to me!'
Ramanna shouted: 'A lie! My father watered it and pruned its branches; it is mine!'

Both men produced contradictory land records, and the village elders were divided into two warring factions.
The King was exhausted: 'If neither will compromise, I shall order the royal woodcutters to saw the tree in half down the middle, so each farmer receives half the timber!'

Venkanna eagerly nodded:
'Yes, Maharaj! A wise verdict! Cut the tree in half! If I cannot have the whole tree, let Ramanna get only half of a dead trunk!'

Ramanna, hearing the decree, threw himself at the King’s feet, weeping bitterly:
'No, Maharaj! I beg of you, do not destroy the tree!
That tree has provided shade to our children and sweet fruit to our families for two generations!
Give the entire tree to Venkanna! Let it live and bear fruit, even if I receive not a single mango!'

King Krishnadevaraya was about to finalize the award when Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, the true owner of the tree has just revealed himself!'

Tenali pointed to Ramanna:
'Look at the two men!
Venkanna was willing to see the living tree destroyed and turned to firewood, because he cares only for selfish spite!
Ramanna was willing to sacrifice his own harvest and give up the tree, because his heart loves the living tree and cannot bear to see it slain!
Only the man who nurtured the tree with love cares for its life!'

King Krishnadevaraya recognized the profound Solomon-like wisdom of Tenali’s deduction.
The King awarded the entire mango tree and the boundary ridge to Ramanna.
Venkanna was fined fifty silver coins for perjury and ordered to plant ten new mango saplings along the public road.
The people praised Tenali’s deep understanding that true love always chooses preservation over destruction.
moral: A parent’s true love protects the welfare of the child, while selfish greed cares only for the prize.
